Steph Curry hinted he may not play against the Phoenix Suns on Saturday, on the second night of a back-to-back, despite the Golden State Warriors dropping to 0-2 after losing 111-108 to the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday. Curry was partly responsible for the loss after going 0-for-4 in the clutch. He finished with 24 points, but shot 33.3% from the field and 3-for-10 from deep.
 The Warriors blew a 12-point lead with 3:47 left, and better decision-making from Curry could have changed the outcome. After a loss like this, the Warriors should be desperate to win against the Suns, but Curry said he probably won't play.
 "Probably not, but I'll talk to the [medical] staff," he said after Friday's loss.
 Fans were disappointed with Steph Curry's plan for Saturday's game, especially after his role in Friday's loss.
 "Completely chokes the game & now this ✌️," one fan said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Steph Curry admits Friday's loss stings more
 The Warriors made no significant roster upgrades despite only 37 wins and a play-in tournament exit last year. They were expected to struggle against good teams, so beating weaker opponents expected to finish in the lottery was crucial.
 However, the Warriors blew one of those winnable games on Friday against the Grizzlies. Steph Curry admitted that while all losses hurt, the Memphis loss stings more.
 "Every game is important," he said. "Especially a home opener after the way that game in LA went, we wanted to bounce back and have a good performance and get a win before the road trip. There are losses and then there are ways that you lose like tonight that sting a bit more."
 The Warriors' schedule isn't getting any easier after Friday. After facing the Suns, potentially without Steph Curry, the Warriors will take on Nikola Jokic's Denver Nuggets, the streaking Minnesota Timberwolves, and the Los Angeles Lakers, who beat them 127-105 in the season opener.
